- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after a price spike (e.g., +5%+ above recent high) — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment turns sharply bullish after a downtrend, model often fails to capture the momentum — increase forecast by 2–5% relative to prior 30d mean.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been above 70.0 for 5+ days, model tends to overpredict; if below 65.0, underpredict — apply a 3–5% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 2–4% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Avoid “overfitting to recent highs” — if last 3 days are above 72.0, don’t forecast >71.5 unless sentiment is >0.80 and rising.
